title: Unified Inference — Pricing & Packaging Notes (v2027-03)
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This document summarizes the recommended pricing and packaging framework for the Unified Inference product line (hosted, Dedicated, and Private) for the 2027 commercial cycle. It describes goals, proposed tiers, billing models, packaging options, migration guidance for existing customers, expected metrics, and launch-rollout steps.

Goals

1. Align pricing with unit economics: reflect per-token and per-embedding cost drivers while providing clear levers for customers to trade off latency, reliability, and cost.
2. Reduce friction for adoption: simple self-serve tiers for early/PLG customers combined with contract-ready offerings for enterprise and Dedicated.
3. Preserve upsell motion: packaging should enable clear expansion paths (Dedicated capacity, Premium SLAs, Optimize add-ons).
4. Ensure predictability for large customers: predictable committed pricing and burst handling for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope

- Products covered: Hosted API (Redwood API), Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem).
- Add-ons: Redwood Console (advanced retention/observability), Redwood Optimize (cost/perf toolkit), Compliance & Audit packages.
- Out of scope: Marketplace reseller agreements, third-party channel-specific discounts (handled by GTM).

Executive summary of recommendations

- Hosted API: Continue usage-based per-token pricing for generation and per-embedding unit pricing for embeddings. Introduce a 3-tier self-serve structure (Developer, Growth, Business) with progressive volume discounts and rate limit increases.
- Dedicated: Offer committed monthly/annual capacity bundles priced per-GPU-hour equivalent with optional burst credits and predictable overage rules. Provide two SKUs: Dedicated Standard and Dedicated Plus (SLA + priority support).
- Private: Enterprise licensing model (platform fee + term-based support & onboarding). Pricing quoted per-deployment with optional managed-services add-on.
- Add-ons & feature bundles: Redwood Optimize sold as tiered subscription (Standard / Advanced) based on evaluation set size and supported quantization profiles. Observability retention and compliance packages priced annually.

Detailed pricing proposals

1) Hosted API — self-serve tiers (suggested list prices, USD)

| Tier | Monthly included credits* | Generation (per 1K tokens) | Embeddings (per 1K units) | Rate limits | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Developer | 100k tokens | $0.0025 | $0.0020 | 5 rps | Free-tier replacement for trial; card required after credits |
| Growth | 5M tokens | $0.0018 | $0.0012 | 25 rps | Popular PLG price point; volume discounts at 50M+ |
| Business | 50M tokens | $0.0011 | $0.0009 | 200 rps | Includes basic support; eligible for sales uplift |

*Included credits are intended to simplify buying decisions; overage billed at list rates with automatic volume-discounting.

Volume discounting rules (hosted)

- 0–5M tokens: list rate
- 5M–50M tokens: 10% off list
- 50M–500M tokens: 25% off list
- 500M+: negotiated enterprise discount

2) Dedicated — committed capacity bundles

Bundle model: customers commit to a monthly GPU-hour equivalent (e.g., 720h per GPU) with a base price per-CPU/GPU-hour. Bundles include a baseline throughput SLAs; overage billed at a transparent per-GPU-hour overage rate.

SKU examples (indicative):
- Dedicated Standard: base price $X per GPU-hour; 99.9% fleet availability SLA; standard support
- Dedicated Plus: +15% on base price; 99.95% availability; 24/7 phone support; dedicated TAM

Bursting and credits

- Offer discretionary burst credits at contract signature (e.g., 10% of committed capacity per month) to handle launch spikes.
- Support configurable autoscaling policies; charges reflect actual GPU usage beyond committed baseline.

3) Private — licensing and professional services

- Platform license: up-front platform fee (one-time) scaled to deployment size (number of nodes / expected concurrency).
- Annual support & maintenance: percentage of license (15%–25%) depending on support SLAs and managed-services inclusion.
- Optional managed services: onboarding, security hardening, air-gap packaging — quoted separately.

Packaging & bundling recommendations

- Core bundle (included in all offerings): Redwood API access, model catalog (standard open models), basic Console metrics (30d retention), standard security controls.
- Optimize bundle (paid add-on): advanced batching/quantization suggestions, quality-monitoring alerts, evaluation harness access.
- Observability add-on: extended retention (90/365 days), per-route tracing, token-level cost breakdown exports.
- Compliance add-on: audit logging retention, SOC/ISO evidence packages, dedicated compliance review sessions.

Migration & upgrade paths

1. Self-serve Hosted -> Dedicated
   - Trigger: sustained usage above 200M tokens/month or customer request for isolation and predictability.
   - Process: sales contact -> sizing workshop (runtime perf profile) -> PO and contract -> onboarding (2–6 weeks).
\2. Dedicated -> Private
   - Trigger: regulatory requirements or on-prem need.
   - Process: pre-sales compliance checklist -> architecture review -> professional services estimate -> migration runbook.

Implementation considerations (billing & platform)

- Metering: ensure per-token/embedding metering is robust and reconciles with model variant (quantized vs FP16) and cache-hit accounting (prefix/KV cache should not double-count tokens).
- Billing granularity: hourly aggregation for Dedicated/Private usage; daily or real-time dashboards for Hosted usage with 24‑hour reconciliation.
- Rate-limiting & throttling: tiered rate limit enforcement in the control plane with configurable burst behavior documented in the SLA.
- Refunds & credits: define clear policies for failed requests, downtime (SLA credits), and accidental overages.

Metrics & success criteria

- Top-line: MRR from Hosted, ARR from Dedicated/Private contracts, % revenue from add-ons.
- Adoption: conversion rate from Developer -> Growth -> Business, number of Dedicated upgrades per quarter.
- Efficiency: revenue per GPU-hour, average gross margin per product line.
- Churn & expansion: net revenue retention target >110% for Dedicated customers in year 1.

Launch & rollout plan

1. Internal alignment (Weeks -4 to 0)
   - Legal finalize terms & SLA language.
   - Finance model validation and topline forecasts.
   - Billing & metering engineering sprint to finalize events and reconciliation pipelines.
\2. Beta (Weeks 0–6)
   - Invite selected Growth/Beta customers to try new tiers and Dedicated SKUs.
   - Instrument telemetry and billing reconciliation; collect early pricing feedback.
\3. Public launch (Week 8)
   - Marketing assets: pricing page, FAQ, calculators, ROI examples.
   - Sales playbook for enterprise deals and Dedicated sizing.
\4. Post-launch (Months 1–6)
   - Evaluate conversion rates, adjust list prices and discount bands if adoption deviates from targets.
   - Optimize discount automation in the billing system.

Open questions / decisions required

- Final list prices for Dedicated per-GPU-hour SKU (requires fleet cost modeling from Eng-Infrastructure).
- Exact Tenant isolation wording in SLA for Dedicated (legal + security review).
- Whether to offer a committed-token bundle for Hosted (customers prefer tokens vs GPU-hours).

Appendix: Example billing events & sample invoices

- Hosted invoice example: line items for generation tokens (billable tokens), embeddings units, Optimize subscription, observability retention.
- Dedicated invoice example: committed capacity subscription (monthly), overage GPU-hours, burst credit adjustments, support surcharge if applicable.

Ownership & next steps

- Product (Ava Martinez): finalize SKUs and public messaging (due 2027-03-08).
- Finance (Elena Kim): finalize ARR/MRR forecasts and coupon/discount policies (due 2027-03-05).
- Eng-infra (Marco Ruiz): confirm metering events and cost-per-GPU models (due 2027-03-04).
- Legal (Priya Desai): finalize SLA language and compliance add-on terms (due 2027-03-07).
